maria: just pushed lumen-slim-v2 int6 build to staging index. did a quick embed eval and seeing a weird short-query recall bump down ~2.8% vs fp32. anyone around to eyeball?
devin: can you paste the eval summary and the exact command you ran?
maria: command:
```
./run_eval.sh --model lumen-slim-v2 --quant int6 --dataset shortquery-v2 --ann hnsw --ef 120 --norm l2
```
summary snippet:
```
baseline fp32: recall@1 = 0.912
this run int6: recall@1 = 0.884  # -0.028
recall@5: 0.965 -> 0.954
mean rank: 2.1 -> 2.35
```

ria: quick checklist: 1) quant backend (onnx/torchscript/our-runtime)? 2) per-channel or per-tensor? 3) was post-processing (whitening/unit-norm) applied same as baseline?
sam: also check idx params; ef=120 might be okay but try ef=250 for recovery. sometimes recall loss from quant can be mitigated by higher ef.
maria: it's our-runtime with int6-per-tensor by default right now. baseline was fp32, unit_norm=True in prod pipeline. i used --norm l2 so should match but maybe normalization got applied twice?
devin: can you dump a few nearest neighbor distances for a tiny subset (first 20 queries) comparing fp32 vs int6? that often shows if distances just shifted vs topology changed.
maria: pasted small csv to the thread (omitted here) — distances are slightly compressed in int6 (gaps smaller).
eval-bot: regression-detected: recall@1 delta=-0.028 on shortquery-v2. severity=medium. auto-ticket ML-4529 created.
ria: try re-run with per-channel quant and ef=250, and also ensure we only normalize once (pass --norm none and rely on stored pipeline). run command:
```
./run_eval.sh --model lumen-slim-v2 --quant int6 --quant-mode per-channel --dataset shortquery-v2 --ann hnsw --ef 250 --norm none
```

maria: re-ran with that exact command. results:
```
recall@1 = 0.908
recall@5 = 0.963
mrr = 0.777
```
looks much closer.
sam: good — seems like per-tensor quant + double/changed normalization + slightly low ef were additive.
devin: action items: 1) change lumen-slim-v2 default quant profile to int6-per-channel in model catalog, 2) add a quick eval smoke in CI that runs shortquery-v2 with ef=250 and asserts recall@1 within -0.02 of fp32, 3) add a small diagnostic CSV export for nearest-neighbor distances to help future triage. i'll file the PRs.
maria: I'll kick off a 5-seed stability sweep (different RNG seeds + index seeds) and post aggregate. thanks all. :rocket:
